newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SKF gains on rationalisation rumours.
newsitem.headline: SKF gains on rationalisation rumours.

text.p: Shares in Swedish ball bearing group SKF rose on the Stockholm bourse on Friday on speculation that the group would present a rationalisation programme in line with Electrolux's plans, dealers said.
At 1400 GMT, the share was up 9.5 crowns at 189.5 while the bourse's general index was 0.48 percent higher.
"Investor has said that it doesn't want shares that don't perform in its portfolio and then SKF also has to show that it can get the share price going," a trader said.
Investor, the powerful Wallenberg family's key investment vehicle, holds 13.3 percent of capital and 30.3 percent of votes in SKF.

Appliance maker Electrolux announced a 2.5 billion crown restructuring programme on Thursday which caused its share to skyrocket. At 1400 GMT, shares in Electrolux were 58 crowns higher at 587, building on a 64 crown Thursday surge.
Investor holds 1.3 percent of Electrolux's capital and 45.2 percent of its votes.
SKF declined to say whether it was planning any restructuring, referring to ongoing cost cuts, and did not want to compare itself with Electrolux.
"A structure is never final," SKF spokesman Lars Malmer said. "The day we need to make any large moves we will announce it."
But he admitted the group was not completely happy with the current structure.
"Costs are still too high," he said.
"It isn't the price that can give us increased profitability but productivity improvements, increased volumes and new products with higher processing value," he said.
"In the long term increased productivity will mean that the space we use for production will decrease," he said. This could mean smaller or fewer plants, he added.
